newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian stocks end mixed, focus on Reliance.
newsitem.headline: Indian stocks end mixed, focus on Reliance.

text.p: Indian share prices ended mixed on Thursday at major bourses, with Reliance Industries hogging market limelight, dealers said.
Reliance rallied 6.0 rupees or 3.18 percent to 194.75 rupees ahead of the petrochemical giant's results for the first half of 1996/97 (April-March) due Friday.
The stock saw volumes of 3.2 million shares at the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE).
The 30-share index of the BSE finished 7.36 points or 0.24 percent higher at 3,112.02 after falling to 3,068.56.
Analysts expect Reliance's net profit to fall 25 percent due to poor market conditions, but some traders say the firm was likely to overcome the shortfall from higher "other income."
"That Reliance's profits will be hit is no news," said trader Ramnik Parikh. "The matter to note is there could be a pleasant surprise."
According to dealers, selective purchases by state-run domestic investment institutions also helped the market recover from an early slide.
Insurance firms and the Unit Trust of India, the country's largest mutual fund were buyers, they said.
SBI gained 1.50 rupees to 210, TISCO 2.0 to 172.50 and BSES 2.75 to 175, while Bajaj Auto shed 4.25 to 926.50 and ACC 18.50 to 1,628.75.
Meanwhile, Delhi shares wiped off early losses to close higher, with the Delhi Stock Exchange index ending 3.92 points or 0.55 percent to 709.93.
The Calcutta exchange index rose 3.79 ponits or 0.91 percent to 420.42.
